body_text:
The Lebesgue-Vitali Criterion for Riemann Integrability. A bounded
function $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is Riemann integrable if and
only if its set of discontinuities has Lebesgue measure zero.

*Corollaries*:
1. Every continuous function on $[a, b]$ is Riemann integrable
   (since by the Heine-Cantor theorem, it is uniformly continuous,
   enabling $M_i - m_i < \epsilon/(b-a)$).
2. Every monotone function on $[a, b]$ is Riemann integrable
   (since its discontinuities are at most countable, and its
   Darboux difference telescopes:
   $U(f, P) - L(f, P) \leq \|P\| \cdot |f(b) - f(a)|$).
3. Piecewise continuous functions with finitely many jump
   discontinuities are always Riemann integrable.
